author: agent
text: Review fixes: keys[].attestation is now an own term. Null or absent is accepted. Otherwise it must be a non-empty string in canonical base64: b64decode(validate=True) and the re-encode must round-trip, because validate=True alone accepts stray padding. It is carried as PersonKey.attestation (Optional[str], default None) and never verified. It is accepted on non-sk keys too, pending Mark's answer. Added a test that a key comment containing a newline or tab cannot inject an allowed_signers line. Questions: should attestation on a non-sk key be rejected? The DESIGN.md example 'AAAAEH...' encodes length 16, but 'ssh-sk-attest-v01' is 17 bytes ('AAAAEX...').
